explanation: Powers quotes Byrd citing Prahl for workplace robbery being an accident arising out of employment; Grace disapproved Prahl only on compensating mental injury without physical injury, a different point.

Proctor (1935) cites Inglish as supporting authority that an employee injured going home with work papers is in the course of employment; Gintert (1934) overruled Inglish on exactly that, and no mention is made.

Creekmore cites Moran alone for malice toward the owner being the gravamen of malicious mischief under section 1760; McDaris (1973) expressly overruled Moran on that element; no negative history noted.

Hausaman mentions the 147 Mo. App. 105 citation (as Purl's Estate) only as appellant's authority on estoppel and holds it inapplicable; Sage overruled Gupton on private-bank separate entity, a different point.

Iyamu relies on Barrett, which quotes Jackson's broad-interpretation maxim for requests for counsel; Montejo overruled Jackson's bar on police-initiated interrogation after arraignment request, not that maxim, and Barrett remains good law.

Coffey cites the Court of Appeals opinion for stating reasons for unequal property division; the Supreme Court on transfer addressed only child support review standard; from memory, remaining issues were summarily affirmed, so the point was not negated.

Stacy cites and quotes the Court of Appeals' Stein opinion for no concurrent jurisdiction under 143-300.1 and 115C-42, though the Supreme Court had reversed that decision outright in 2006; no subsequent history is noted; different litigation.
